articles.title: F1 star Lewis Hamilton visits Gaza border
articles.description: F1 star Lewis Hamilton visits Gaza border Formula One star Lewis Hamilton visited Egypt's Rafah border crossing on Tuesday and met aid workers delivering assistance to the war-battered Gaza Strip, according to an Egyptian government statement. North Sinai governor "Khaled Megawer took Lewis Hamilton on a visit to the Rafah land crossing to learn about the Egyptian efforts to support the Palestinian brothers in the Gaza Strip", the statement read. articles.title: Israeli fire kills seven, including a father and son, in Gaza
articles.description: Israeli fire kills seven, including a father and son, in Gaza Israeli forces killed at least seven Palestinians, including a father and his 13-year-old son, in the Gaza Strip on Tuesday, local health officials said. Medics said Fadi Rajab and his son Abubakr were killed in an air strike that hit the roof of a displacement shelter in the Zeitoun neighbourhood in Gaza City. A third Palestinian was killed in an Israeli air strike near a school in Gaza City's Daraj neighbourhood, health officials added. In Khan Younis, in southern Gaza, Israeli gunfire killed a man, medics said. Later on Tuesday, an Israeli air strike hit a metal foundry in the Sabra neighbourhood of Gaza City, killing three people, medics said, taking the day's death toll to at least seven.

articles.description: Anti-Muslim influence campaign targeting UK traced back to Israel A new investigation has traced a major anti-Muslim propaganda campaign targeting Britain back to Israel . The campaign, uncovered by academics Marc Owen Jones and Sohan Dsouza, was at its height before the UK's 2024 general election and the anti-Muslim riots that raged across the country later that year. articles.description: As heavy rains swamp Gaza's tents, Israel must face sanctions It took a mere dozen hours of the first winter storm to flood around 70,000 tents in Gaza. Nothing about this should surprise anyone who has paid even the scantest attention to the humanitarian situation in Gaza. Every year, Palestinians in the coastal enclave face the threat of flooding due to winter rains. articles.description: Nearly 80 percent of Britons see Israel as a threat to world peace Nearly four in five Britons see Israel as a serious threat to world peace, according to a survey published last week by the National Centre for Social Research (NatCen). The figure rose from 48 percent in 2005 to 78 percent this spring, two-and-a-half years into the genocide in Gaza and just after Israel and the US had attacked Iran. articles.title: Gaza sandbank collapse kills five amid heavy rains
articles.description: Gaza sandbank collapse kills five amid heavy rains At least five people have been killed, including three children, after heavy rains caused a sandbank to collapse in central Gaza's Deir al-Balah, Wafa news reported on Sunday. A civil defence spokesman added that five wounded people had been pulled out of the rubble after their tents were hit, and teams are continuing to search for survivors. The incident comes amid worsening conditions faced by displaced Palestinians in Gaza, as national and internation institutions warned heavy rainfall and bad weather require urgent intervention and the provision of safe shelter and winter supplies.
